title: WASSCE Further Maths: Calculus (Differentiation & Integration) - Further Mathematics - Definite Integrals
subject: Further Mathematics

questions.explain: The anti-derivative of $3x^2$ is $x^3$. Evaluating this from $x = 1$ to $x = 2$ gives $[2^3] - [1^3] = 8 - 1 = 7$.
questions.subject: Further Mathematics

questions.explain: Rewrite as $\int_1^4 (x^{1/2} + x^{-1/2}) dx$. The integral is $[\frac{2}{3}x^{3/2} + 2x^{1/2}]_1^4$. Evaluate at upper limit $x=4$: $\frac{2}{3}(8) + 2(2) = \frac{16}{3} + 4 = \frac{28}{3}$. Evaluate at lower limit $x=1$: $\frac{2}{3}(1) + 2(1) = \frac{8}{3}$. Subtracting gives $\frac{28}{3} - \frac{8}{3} = \frac{20}{3}$.

questions.explain: The anti-derivative of $\sec^2 x$ is $\tan x$. Evaluating from $x = 0$ to $x = \pi/4$ yields $\tan(\pi/4) - \tan(0)$. Since $\tan(\pi/4) = 1$ and $\tan(0) = 0$, the result is $1 - 0 = 1$.

questions.q: Calculate the exact value of $\int_{-1}^1 (1-x) dx$.
questions.explain: The anti-derivative is $x - \frac{x^2}{2}$. Evaluating from $-1$ to $1$: Upper limit gives $1 - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{2}$. Lower limit gives $-1 - \frac{1}{2} = -\frac{3}{2}$. Subtracting the lower limit value from the upper limit value gives $\frac{1}{2} - (\frac{-3}{2}) = \frac{1}{2} + \frac{3}{2} = 2$.
